newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state sells majority in Helwan.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state sells majority in Helwan.

text.p: The Egyptian government announced in state-run newspapers on Sunday it had sold a 22.3 percent stake in Helwan Portland Cement and relinquished its majority stake in the already part-privatised firm.
Last week, the Holding Company offered to auction at least 10 percent or 2.5 million shares in Helwan Cement but sold instead the 22.3 percent, equivalent to 5.584 million shares.
Share prices were fixed at 56.50 pounds and the new buyers included international and local funds, sources close to the deal said.
The sale put 52.1 percent of Helwan Cement's equity in private hands. Individuals and funds already hold 29.8 percent.
The state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories owns the remaining 47.9 percent.
On Sunday, Helwan Cement shares were trading at 66.00 pounds, up 0.75 pounds from Thursday's close.
Helwan Cement increased net profits for financial year 1995/96 to 125.52 million pounds ($36.9 million) from 103.61 million a year earlier.
The financial year ended on June 30. Net profits in the first quarter of 96/97 were 35 million pounds.
The firm, one of Egypt's leading cement manufacturers, said earlier it was raising dividends for 1995/96 to five pounds from the 4.75 pounds it had promised investors earlier this year.
Dividends for 1994/95 were four pounds per share.
The firm's net sales rose to 550.57 million pounds from 495.73 million in 1994/95.
